summary: One method call advances one fixed-size Date value by one UTC calendar day and formats one fixed-width calendar-date string, so the work is constant per invocation.

optimality.argument: Producing the result of one method invocation necessarily returns one value and therefore requires Omega(1) work. The implementation copies one Date, performs one UTC calendar-field update, converts the result once, and extracts a fixed-width prefix, establishing O(1) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: Every invocation must inspect its receiver and return a date string, requiring at least constant work.
The accepted source performs a fixed sequence of Date operations and a fixed-width string extraction, with no input-sized loop or recursion.
Authored and Node-verified cases cover ordinary dates, month and year rollovers, leap-day entry and exit, a non-leap century, and the Unix epoch boundary.
